# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — Host DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR

**Evidence reviewed:** `2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (only artifact present in the evidence folder; no separate IDS/Suricata export was provided). Capture spans 2026-02-28 23:55:06 to 2026-03-01 04:16:35 (~4h21m), 15,512 packets.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.2.28.88 |
| MAC address | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (confirmed via DHCP option 12 and NBNS name registration) |
| AD domain | EASYAS123.TECH (DC: EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech, 10.2.28.2) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **brolf** (Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, realm EASYAS123.TECH) |

## Malware family

**NetSupport Manager RAT** (NetSupport Client abused as a commodity RAT).

**Attribution basis: signature-confirmed**, not behavioral inference. The traffic contains the literal NetSupport RAT protocol markers in cleartext:

- HTTP `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` on every outbound request in the C2 session.
- POST bodies to a static URI `/fakeurl.htm` carrying the well-documented NetSupport RAT field set: `CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1` (client heartbeat) and `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<encrypted blob>` (encrypted command/response channel).
- Traffic runs over destination TCP port 443 but the protocol is plaintext HTTP (`http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm`, not TLS) — a known evasion trait of this NetSupport RAT campaign to blend with normal HTTPS port usage.

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in this capture)

**Command-and-control:**
- `45.131.214.85:443` — C2 server, plaintext HTTP masquerading on port 443. 264 POST beacons observed from 2026-02-28 23:55:51 to 2026-03-01 04:16:28 (~4h20m, roughly one beacon per 60s), URI `/fakeurl.htm`.

**Malicious domain:**
- `vadusa.xyz` — resolved by the victim to 45.131.214.85 immediately before the first C2 beacon.

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` (NetSupport RAT POLL/ENCD C2 endpoint)

**Likely infection vector (circumstantial, grounded in timing):**
- Victim resolved and connected via TLS to `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (23.64.147.24, legitimate Akamai-hosted government IP) at 23:55:50–23:55:51, seconds before the first NetSupport beacon at 23:55:51.530968. This timing is consistent with the known NetSupport RAT distribution pattern (fake-CAPTCHA/"ClickFix" lure spoofing or piggybacking on the FMCSA site), but because that session is TLS-encrypted, the lure page content and the actual dropper delivery URL are not visible in this capture — this point is behavioral/circumstantial, not signature-confirmed.

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- None recoverable. No cleartext HTTP object in the capture (`tshark --export-objects http`) matches an executable, script, or installer; all extracted HTTP objects are benign Microsoft/MSN/Adobe/Nvidia telemetry beacons unrelated to the intrusion. The NetSupport client installer itself was either already present on the host before capture start or delivered over the encrypted TLS session noted above — no file name or SHA256 can be grounded in this evidence.

## Summary

DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), used by domain user `brolf` on the EASYAS123.TECH AD domain, is compromised with NetSupport Manager RAT. The malware beacons every ~60 seconds to `45.131.214.85:443` (domain `vadusa.xyz`) via plaintext HTTP POST to `/fakeurl.htm`, using the RAT's native `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` protocol, for the full duration of the capture. All other traffic in the capture (AD/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB to the DC 10.2.28.2, Microsoft/Adobe/MSN telemetry, Windows Update) is normal enterprise workstation background noise and not part of the incident.
